GROCERIES

Help paying for food

Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), sometimes called food stamps. Benefits are provided on a payment card for eligible food purchases.

QUESTIONS YOU SHOULDN’T HAVE TO GUESS AT

Let’s clear a few things up.

Is this an application?

No. This is an independent starting point. We help you identify a program to check and link to official tools. The relevant agency decides eligibility and processes applications.

Can I qualify if I have a job?

Possibly. Nutrition assistance uses household income and other criteria; having a job alone is not a disqualification. Check the official tool for your circumstances. [8]

My child isn’t a baby anymore. Is it too late?

The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children can serve eligible children until their fifth birthday. Use the check above or the official eligibility tool. [8]

Can I check even if I already get other benefits?

Yes. Receiving Medicaid, food assistance, or certain cash assistance may help establish income eligibility for the women’s and children’s nutrition program. Other requirements still apply. [8]

Will you store or share my answers?

No. This checker runs in this page and does not send or save your answers. Following an official link opens that service, which has its own privacy practices.

What if the checker says my income is above the guide?

That is not a denial. Some other benefits provide an income-eligibility pathway; household counting and income exclusions can also matter. Use the official tool or ask a local agency before assuming you cannot qualify.

Why do people miss benefits they could receive?

Research has documented confusion about eligibility, difficulty finding time for clinic visits, and scheduling or transportation problems. Some people report other support or less need. A participation gap alone cannot tell us which explanation applies. [2] [3]

YOUR PATH / TAX CREDITS

Check a credit
for people who work.

This is separate from food benefits. Use the Internal Revenue Service’s questionnaire to check the Earned Income Tax Credit for the tax year you select.

TAX REFUND

A tax credit for people who work

Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC). Working does not automatically put this help out of reach.

≈22%of eligible taxpayers did not participate in tax year 2022, using the reported national estimate. [5]

You need to file to claim it, even if you don’t normally have to file a return. [6]

Use the official tax-credit checker ↗

What happens next?

  1. Open the official checker and select your tax year.
  2. Answer its questions about income and household circumstances.
  3. If eligible, claim the credit through your tax return. The checker itself does not file a return.

SOURCES & NOTES

Check the numbers.

Where the figures come from, how they were calculated, and what they cannot tell us.

Definitions, calculations & limitations

Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC): 11,829,215 estimated eligible people − 6,631,309 participants = 5,197,906, displayed as 5.20 million. Participants ÷ eligible people = 56.0587%, rounded to 56.1%. The U.S. Department of Agriculture calls this the coverage rate. Participation generally means enrollment and receipt or pickup of benefits, with specified breastfeeding mother/infant exceptions; it does not measure full food redemption.

Eligibility is modeled from survey data and adjustments, not an individually verified census. The national total includes U.S. territories. Estimates describe an average month in 2023, not today's caseload. [1]

Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP): estimates combine administrative participation records with modeled eligibility. The study excludes certain recipients outside federal income/resource limits, Disaster SNAP, and benefits received in error. Do not combine these percentages with unadjusted caseload counts. [4]

Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC): 100% − the Current Population Survey-based national estimate of 78% = approximately 22% nonparticipation. The Internal Revenue Service also publishes an American Community Survey-based 80.8% estimate for its state table. Different underlying surveys produce different estimates; this project uses the figure the Internal Revenue Service identifies as its reported national estimate. [5]

Causes and populations: no claim is made that all nonparticipation is caused by administrative barriers. The 2024 WIC study used an interrupted, nonrepresentative sample and measured income at interview, not necessarily at exit. This version does not present a racial or ethnic comparison; that requires separate attention to category definitions and uncertainty. [2]
